frequency_question: How often does Congress successfully block a submitted executive nuclear or arms sales agreement via joint resolution of disapproval within the statutory window?
membership_rule: Includes all formal 123 agreements for nuclear cooperation and major arms sales notifications submitted to Congress under statutory review provisions since 1976. Excludes informal agreements or treaties requiring standard 2/3 Senate ratification.
window: 323 days matching the specific review and statutory constraints
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 4 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 4 named major high-stakes foreign policy disapproval battles; believed complete for major nuclear and Middle East arms agreements facing active disapproval resolutions.
known_gaps: Minor notifications that never reached floor votes due to withdrawal are excluded from the denominator of active challenge attempts, though including them would lower the hit rate further.
skeleton: 4 historical major congressional disapproval challenges against executive foreign/nuclear/arms agreements involving veto-proof thresholds
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks governing congressional review of international agreements (AEA Section 123) remain stable over multi-decade periods.
